disagreements.title: short-circuit impedance transformer pandapower
disagreements.argument_include: Short-circuit is an under-represented, high-value out-of-scenario theme. A faithful task exists: build a small net with a transformer, run calc_sc, report the short-circuit current (ikss_ka) downstream of the transformer. Network is unspecified -> §2.2c permits a self-built net (round-1 kept several custom_feeder_sc items).
disagreements.argument_exclude: The title/excerpt are ambiguous between (a) a demand for a computed short-circuit RESULT (ikss) and (b) a modelling/parameter question about the transformer's short-circuit IMPEDANCE (vk/vkr) — reading (b) is a parameterisation-curiosity exclusion. The 22-word excerpt ('I am a student... I have') gives no target quantity, so choosing one risks authoring the target backward.
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom small net (ext_grid -> transformer -> LV bus), pp.shortcircuit.calc_sc(fault='3ph'), report res_bus_sc.ikss_ka at the LV bus.

expert_verdict.basis: Full original post retrieved: the author asks for the INTERNAL short-circuit impedance / magnetising admittance values pandapower derives from the nameplate vk/vkr/pfe/i0 parameters - a result-extraction demand, not a parameterisation curiosity.
expert_verdict.build_correction: Corrected sketch: no calc_sc. Build a transformer from nameplate parameters and extract the internally derived per-unit branch impedance magnitude via the deterministic internal branch representation.

disagreements.title: Frequency control in AC power flow calculation?
disagreements.argument_include: pandapower does support a distributed-slack AC power flow (runpp(distributed_slack=True) with gen slack_weight), which is the concrete feature that answers this question. A unique task exists: build a net with two weighted gens, run distributed-slack pf, report one gen's active power (the frequency-response split).
disagreements.argument_exclude: Mapping 'frequency control' -> 'distributed slack' is interpretive: primary frequency response and pandapower's steady-state distributed-slack are not the same object, so the rewrite would drift the analysis-type element (one of the 4 frozen semantics). The original is phrased as a capability question ('is there any built-in method').
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom 3-bus, 2 gens with slack_weight, pp.runpp(net, distributed_slack=True), report res_gen.p_mw of the non-reference gen.

expert_verdict.basis: Full post confirms a built-in-method demand answered by weighted slack distribution in the AC power flow; the interpretive gap is acceptable under the four-element rule.
expert_verdict.build_correction: None - original sketch maintained (3-bus, two weighted gens, distributed-slack pf, non-reference gen p_mw).

disagreements.title: Control strategy for multiple OLTC-coupled transformer
disagreements.argument_include: Tap control is convertible and round-1 already used ContinuousTapControl: build a net with a tap-changing transformer whose controller holds a bus voltage setpoint, run pf, report the settled tap position or controlled-bus voltage.
disagreements.argument_exclude: The question is explicitly about the coupled-control STRATEGY between MULTIPLE OLTC transformers ('enquire on the strategy used') — a mechanism-curiosity framing, and coupled multi-tap coordination has no single canonical pandapower solution (uniqueness risk, cf. #1527).
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom HV/MV net, 2 transformers with ContinuousTapControl to a shared setpoint, pp.runpp, report a controlled-bus vm_pu (single-transformer reduction to preserve uniqueness).

expert_verdict.basis: Full text confirms mechanism curiosity about the coupled multi-OLTC control strategy; no unique task.

disagreements.title: Unbalanced voltage references for three phase asymmetrical power flow in LV grids
disagreements.argument_include: Three-phase/unbalanced is a valuable out-of-scenario theme (only 4 in the n=84 set). A faithful 3ph task exists: build a small unbalanced LV feeder, run runpp_3ph, report the lowest per-phase voltage.
disagreements.argument_exclude: The specific novel ask is setting UNBALANCED voltage REFERENCES at the slack — pandapower's ext_grid in runpp_3ph uses a balanced positive-sequence source, so the exact demand may be feature-limited; a faithful rewrite might have to drop the 'unbalanced references' element (four-element preservation risk).
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom small LV feeder with per-phase asymmetric_load, pp.runpp_3ph, report min over res_bus_3ph.vm_a/b/c_pu.

expert_verdict.basis: Feature-gap: ext_grid does not support per-phase unbalanced voltage references; a faithful rewrite is impossible.

disagreements.title: Balanced and unbalanced short circuit voltage of transformer
disagreements.argument_include: Electrical-Engineering.SE is a prized platform for source diversity (0 built so far); the topic (transformer balanced vs unbalanced short-circuit behaviour) can be pointed at a pandapower calc_sc task with balanced vs single-phase faults.
disagreements.argument_exclude: The post is a power-systems THEORY question ('where to start', positive/zero sequence of a transformer's short-circuit voltage) that merely mentions pandapower in full-text; converting it to a fault-current demand changes the analysis type and target quantity (four-element drift). It reads as an open-ended discussion with no concrete pandapower output quantity.
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom 3ph net with a transformer, calc_sc for 3ph vs 1ph faults, report the ratio or one ikss_ka.

expert_verdict.basis: Theory question. Conservative ruling on the stored excerpt - full text unreachable (site blocks fetching from this environment).

disagreements.title: How to change per unit base before power flow calculation
disagreements.argument_include: Prized EE.SE platform. Convertible reading: parameterise a transformer/grid with quantities given on one per-unit base, build the net so pandapower's internal base is consistent, run pf, report a per-unit bus voltage.
disagreements.argument_exclude: The core ask is a per-unit base-change THEORY/derivation question (pandapower handles p.u. internally, so there is no user-facing 'change the base' operation); a faithful pandapower demand with a unique output quantity is hard to author without inventing the task. Reads as modelling-curiosity.
disagreements.if_included_build_sketch: custom 2-bus with a transformer parameterised from nameplate data, pp.runpp, report res_bus.vm_pu at the LV bus.

expert_verdict.basis: Theory question (per-unit base-change derivation). Conservative ruling on the stored excerpt - full text unreachable (site blocks fetching from this environment).
